sentences.text: Labdhu Ram vs . Sh. Amandeep Garag & Ors. on 11 March, 2025

Author: Jyotsna Rewal Dua
Bench: Jyotsna Rewal Dua
Labdhu Ram Vs. Sh. Amandeep Garag & Ors.
Copc No.471 of 2024 11.03.2025 Present: Mr. Romesh Verma, Senior Advocate with Mr. Sumit
Sharma, Advocate, for the petitioner. Ms. Menka Raj Chauhan, Deputy Advocate General, for the
respondents.
This petition is with the grievance that the judgment rendered in Cwp No.6581 of 2021 (Labdhu
Ram Versus State of H.P. & others), decided on 28.06.2023, has been violated by the respondents.

Operative portion of the aforesaid judgment reads as under:-
"19.

In view of the above settled legal position, we are of the opinion that the stand of the State that it need not pay any compensation for utilizing the petitioner's land for the purpose of laying a road cannot be countenanced and the State is bound to pay market value compensation to the petitioner for utilizing his land for the purpose of the road.

20. Therefore, the writ petition is allowed with costs of Rs.10,000/- and a direction is issued to the respondents to demarcate the land of the petitioner utilized for the purpose of the road in question within four weeks, treat it as having been acquired for the said purpose and pay him the highest amount towards compensation among compensation under the awards Annexures P-3 and P-4 with all statutory benefits under the Land Acquisition Act,1894 within eight weeks."
2. Notice of this contempt petition was waived for the respondents on 20.08.2024, when compliance affidavit/reply was directed to be filed within three weeks.

After taking two further opportunities,
respondent No.1 filed reply.

Taking note of this reply, following order was passed in this petition on 27.11.2024:-
"The only stand taken by respondent No.1 in its reply is that respondents are in the process of filing Special Leave Petition against the decision rendered in CWP No.6581 of 2021 (Labdhu Ram vs. State of H.P. & Ors.) decided on 28.06.2023.

sentences.text:
However,
mere intention to file an SLP, without an actual SLP having been filed and without the judgment sought to be enforced having been stayed, give no justification to the respondents for not implementing the judgment.

Learned Deputy Advocate General seeks and is allowed final opportunity of two weeks to implement the decision and file compliance affidavit in that regard, failing Labdhu Ram vs . Sh. Amandeep Garag & Ors.

1 which appropriate order shall be passed in the matter.
List after two weeks."
3. At the request of learned counsel appearing for the respondents, the matter was adjourned twice thereafter.
When the matter was taken up on 27.02.2025, it was again adjourned at the request of learned Deputy Advocate General to enable the respondents to comply with the judgment in letter and spirit.
4. During the course of hearing today, learned Deputy Advocate General pleads no instructions.
Learned Deputy Advocate General also submits that the judgment alleged to have been violated by the respondents is still in force and has not been stayed.

That being the position and the admitted fact that the judgment in question has still not been implemented, prima facie, respondents No.1 to 3 appears to have committed the contempt by violating the directions issued in Labdhu Ram's case.
Let show cause notice be issued to respondents No.1 to 3 as to why proceedings under the Contempt of Courts Act be not drawn against them for violating the directions issued in Labdhu Ram's case.
Notice be made returnable for 26.03.2025.
Reply to the show cause notice be furnished by the respondents before the next date of hearing.
